key_insight: A physics-informed Fourier-wavelet transformer reconstructs next-step CFD velocity fields more accurately across multiple flow scales by combining hybrid spectral encoding, PDE-aware attention, and self-supervised pretraining.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical surrogate modeling path for faster CFD prediction while preserving localized wake physics that are often missed by global-only or standard neural surrogate methods.
method: Hybrid Fourier-wavelet spectral encoding captures both global trends and localized multiscale structures.
Physics-biased self-attention is guided by PDE residual diagnostics to emphasize physically consistent features.
Self-supervised pretraining uses Masked Physics Prediction and Equation Consistency Prediction before downstream reconstruction.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on cylinder-wake and fluid-structure-interaction benchmarks under a shared local protocol, the model achieved the best aggregate results, including NRMSE 0.05875 and PCC 0.97019 on cylinder wake and NRMSE 2.70×10^-4 on FSI.
watch_item: The method is benchmarked on two specific real-world cases, so generalization, stability, and cost on larger or more diverse CFD settings still need validation.
paper_title: A Physics-Informed Fourier-Wavelet Transformer for Multiscale Computational Fluid Dynamics Surrogate Modeling
